summary: Explains accessing dict values with bracket or dot notation; bracket notation always works, while dot notation fails for keys colliding with Python dict/str attributes (like keys, items, get, update) or dunder names.
questions: Should I use dot or bracket notation for dictionary keys?
Why does foo.keys not return my key's value?
Which dictionary keys can't be used with dot notation?

answer_card.title: Bracket vs dot notation for dictionaries
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
foo['field1']
foo.field1
```

Bracket notation **always works**. Dot notation breaks when the key collides with Python attributes or methods (e.g. `keys`, `items`, `values`, `get`, `update`, `copy`, `count`, `index`, `pop`, `split`, `format`, ...) or starts and ends with `__`. Use brackets for those.
